Hanna: Quick triage: rk-alpha-ptq shows anchor NDCG +1.7% but MRR -2.6% on sampled_holdout. Canary CTR -1.1%. This feels like label alignment / dedupe mismatch rather than pure quality. Anyone free?
Owen: Can you summarize pipeline differences between offline eval and prod sampler? Small mismatches often cause label-to-id drift.
Hanna: Offline eval does dedupe at candidate ingestion (dedupe.threshold=0.9) and then stable sort. Prod dedupes later in the serving pipeline with threshold 0.85 and applies a freshness shuffle.
Kai: That could explain it: offline labels are tied to original candidate ids. If prod dedupe removes the labeled winner, online CTR drops even if reranker score is fine.
Miriam: Also verify that candidate canonicalization (url normalization / trailing slash stripping) is identical. We had a mismatch before where anchors used normalized ids and prod used raw.
Hanna: Good call. I ran a short probe: replayed 2k sampled requests through prod sampler but kept labels tied to original ids -> 28 cases where the labeled winner got removed by prod dedupe.
Owen: 28/2k is significant. That could explain MRR down. Two quick mitigations: (1) align dedupe thresholds for canary, (2) bind labels to canonicalized signatures upstream before any dedupe.
Kai: For longer term, we should generate a "label-preserving replica" of candidate pools in eval: apply the exact prod pipeline and then transfer labels by matching content hashes, not candidate indices. That will catch this earlier.
Miriam: I opened ticket #3321: "label-to-id leakage when deduping" and added repro job 7043211122 (replay+hash-match). Also adding a CI test that runs a 1k replay and asserts label retention >= 99.5%.
EvalBot: Job 7043211122 queued: replay-hash-match (seed=9).
Hanna: Quick numbers from the replay: label retention after prod dedupe = 97.6%. When I re-scored only the retained examples, MRR gap closes to -0.4% and NDCG still +1.6%.
Owen: That nails it. CTR likely dropped because some labeled good answers were removed upstream. Recommend we pause rollout until canary dedupe threshold matches eval and we have canonicalization in place.
Kai: I'll add a small shim to compute content-hash signatures during candidate generation and persist them with labels. Then any downstream dedupe must preserve entries with labeled hashes. Quick patch PR #1502.
Miriam: I'll schedule a short canary with dedupe.threshold=0.9 and canonical-hash-protect enabled. Deploy window 30m. Monitor CTR and label retention.
Hanna: Thanks all. Lesson: always validate label preservation through the full serving pipeline for quantized bring-ups. Adding to the onboarding checklist now. :white_check_mark:
